hindi: जिसकी बोलते समय छाती ऊपर की ओर बहुत दुखती है
english: He whose chest, while he speaks, aches greatly upward
notes: Part of a list of signs that is gathered up in unit 43 ('all of those are ripened by time'). 'vadataḥ' is a genitive participle, 'of one speaking'. 'ūrdhvam' is taken as an adverb, 'upward'.

hindi: जिसका उच्छ्वास यानी बाहर निकलती साँस बहुत लम्बी, बहुत छोटी, दुर्गन्ध वाली अथवा सुगन्ध वाली
english: He whose exhalation (ucchvāsa) is too long, too short, foul-smelling or sweet-smelling
notes: Part of the list gathered up in unit 43. Printed 'gaṃdhi' is normalised to gandhi (orthographic, recorded once). The line has no verb; the sentence runs on.

words.gram: pass. pres. part. ā-√yam, f. nom. pl.

words.gloss: in sneezing, going, urinating and the like

hindi: जिसकी उँगलियाँ खींचे जाने पर न चटकें, और जिसका अलग-अलग भी शब्द छींकने, गमन, मूत्रत्याग आदि में अपनी स्वाभाविक अवस्था से परे हो
english: He whose fingers, when stretched, would not crack, and whose sound, even 'other and other' (reading doubtful), in sneezing, going, urinating and the like, is beyond its natural state

text_flags.why: possible: 'anyo'nyo'pi' (anyaḥ anyaḥ api) gives a poor sense; the intended word may be different (e.g. anyonyam api); no firm correction can be made, so the printed reading is kept in words

notes: Two clauses (yasya twice). 'āyamyamānā' = nom. pl. f. before voiced 'n' (āḥ drops visarga: regular). 'anyo'nyo'pi' is read literally as anyaḥ anyaḥ api; doubtful, so the translation marks it. 'gata' in kṣuta-gata-mūtraṇa is taken as 'going'; another sense (e.g. passing wind) cannot be excluded. The sentence continues; see unit 43. The Hindi 'हो' / 'चटकें' reflect the optative sphuṭeyuḥ in the first clause only.

words.gloss: smell of garlands, fruits, sandalwood (standard), corpses and the like
in body, mouth, waste (mala), wound, clothes and the like

hindi: जिसके शरीर, मुख, मल, व्रण यानी घाव, वस्त्र आदि में माला, फल, चन्दन, शव आदि की प्रिय अथवा अप्रिय गन्ध
english: He in whose body, mouth, waste (mala), wound, clothes and the like there is a smell, pleasant or unpleasant, of garlands, fruits, sandalwood, corpses and the like
notes: Part of the list gathered up in unit 43. kuṇapa = corpse (also 'carrion'). mala here is read as bodily waste (doctrinal term kept); another division of deha-mukha-mala cannot be excluded. candana = sandalwood, Santalum album (standard). The line has no verb.

hindi: जिसके शरीर को विरूपता अथवा सुरसता के कारण जूँ, मक्खी आदि बहुत छोड़ देती हैं या उसका आश्रय लेती हैं
english: He whose body, because of deformity (vairūpya) or good flavour (saurasya), lice, flies and the like greatly abandon or resort to
notes: 'atyartham' is taken with the verbs ('greatly'); it could instead qualify vairūpya/saurasya ('excessive'). The text does not say which cause goes with abandoning and which with resorting. 'yūkā' for yūkāḥ is regular sandhi; the avagraha printed in 'vā'tyartham' is a print habit (ā + a). Sentence continues; see unit 43.

words.gloss: excessive coldness resembling kumuda (probably white water lily, Nymphaea, probable) and utpala (probably blue water lily, Nymphaea nouchali, probable)
in (parts) whose flesh and blood have gone

hindi: जिसके सदा गर्म रहने वाले अंगों और अवयवों में ठण्डक, अथवा ठण्डे अंगों में कुमुद यानी सम्भवतः श्वेत कुमुदिनी और उत्पल यानी सम्भवतः नीलकमल जैसी अत्यन्त शीतलता, अत्यधिक पसीना, अत्यधिक अकड़न, और जैसे मांस और रक्त चले गए हों ऐसे अंगों में ढीलापन
english: He in whom there is coldness in the limbs and parts that are constantly warm, or, in those that are (already) cold, excessive coldness resembling kumuda (probably white water lily) and utpala (probably blue water lily), excessive sweating, excessive stiffness, and slackness as if in (parts) whose flesh and blood have gone

text_flags.why: possible: 'straṃsa' is not a standard word; sraṃsa (slipping, slackness) fits the sense and the other signs

notes: Part of the list gathered up in unit 43. Identifications: kumuda = white water lily / night lotus, Nymphaea (probable); utpala = blue water lily, Nymphaea nouchali (probable); only a comparison of coldness is meant. 'sraṃsa' is kept broad (slackness, loosening). 'satatoṣmasu' read as satata-uṣman, locative plural. 'śīteṣu' taken as 'in cold (ones)' with aṅgāvayaveṣu understood. The line has no verb.

hindi: और जिसके शरीर में महाभूतों का योग या अतियोग एक साथ दिखाई देता है, वे सभी कालपक्व यानी काल से पके हुए हैं
english: And he in whose body a conjunction (yoga) or excessive conjunction (atiyoga) of the great elements (mahābhūta) is seen at one time: all those are ripened by time (kālapakva)
notes: Closing 'iti' marks the end of the preceding list of signs (units 37-43); not translated. 'yoga' is kept as literal 'conjunction'; the text does not say here what is joined, and the sense (union with, or an abnormal combination of, the elements) is not decided. 'te' (all those) refers back to the persons described in the list. 'kāla-pakva' kept literal.

hindi: और इस विषय में है
english: And on this point there is
notes: Introductory formula ('bhavati cātra') that opens the verse(s) which follow; the thing that 'is' is not named in the line, so nothing is supplied.

hindi: जिसकी सिराओं यानी नसों की रेखाएँ पहले कभी न देखी हुई, अथवा बालचन्द्र के समान भी
english: He whose vein-lines (sirā, vein) are unprecedented, or even like the young moon
notes: The sentence is completed by the next unit (the places and the six months). 'sirā' = vein, vessel (probable; a general term for blood vessels). 'bāla-indu' = young (crescent) moon. The line has no verb. 'sirālekhā' = sirālekhāḥ (regular sandhi before voiced b).

words.gloss: at the head of the bladder (basti, bladder)

hindi: ललाट पर अथवा बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय के शीर्ष पर, वह छह मास नहीं जीता
english: On the forehead, or at the head of the bladder (basti), he does not live six months
notes: Completes the sentence begun in unit 45 ('whose vein-lines ...'). 'bastiśīrṣa' is kept literal ('head of the bladder'); which part is meant (upper part of the bladder, or the lower abdomen above it) is not fixed by the text. 'ṣaṇmāsān' accusative of duration, 'for six months'.

words.gloss: like a lotus leaf (padminī, lotus plant, Nelumbo nucifera, standard)

hindi: जिस देहधारी के शरीर में जल कमलिनी के पत्ते के समान
english: Water, as with a lotus (padminī) leaf, in the body of whichever embodied being
notes: The verb is in the next unit ('plavate'). Whether 'vat' compares the water's behaviour on a lotus leaf is understood but not stated, so the translation stays close to the words.

hindi: तैरता है; तैरने वाले का, उसका जीवन छह मास है
english: It floats; of one that floats, his life is six months
notes: Continues unit 47 ('water ... in the body of whichever embodied being'). 'plavamānasya' (of one floating) is difficult: it may refer to the water or to the person; the translation keeps it literal. Copula understood ('is').

hindi: जिसकी सिराएँ यानी नसें हरी-सी आभा वाली और रोमकूप बन्द
english: He whose veins (sirā) are of greenish appearance and whose hair pores are closed
notes: The printed 'yasyaromakūpāśca' is yasya roma-kūpāḥ ca with the space missing (a spacing matter, not a letter error). 'saṃvṛta' can mean closed or covered; 'closed' is chosen. Completed by the next unit. 'harita' = green or yellowish-green.

hindi: वह खट्टे की इच्छा करने वाला पुरुष पित्त से मृत्यु को प्राप्त होता है
english: That man, craving the sour (amla), attains death from Pitta
notes: Completes the sentence of unit 49. 'amla' is the sour taste. 'pittāt' is ablative, 'from/because of Pitta'. pitta is neuter.

hindi: जिसके सिर पर अथवा मुख पर भी गोबर के चूर्ण के समान चूर्ण
english: He on whose head, or even on the face, there is powder resembling powder of cow dung

text_flags.why: possible: neuter nominative needs the anusvāra; the final -m seems dropped in print

notes: The line has no verb; the sentence runs into unit 52 ('or oily smoke on the head ...'). 'mūrdhni' is the locative of mūrdhan.

words.gloss: up to the end of a month

hindi: सिर पर चिकनाई वाला धुआँ, अथवा; उसका जीवन मास के अन्त तक है
english: Smoke with oiliness on the head, or; his life is up to the end of a month
notes: 'vā' is read with the preceding unit's alternatives ('powder on the head ... or oily smoke on the head'); the last clause gives the life span for the signs. 'sasnehaṃ' is neuter while dhūma is masculine, so it is taken as an adverb, 'with oiliness'. 'vāmāsāṃtaṃ' = vā + māsa-antam is a reading; another division is possible. Copula understood.

hindi: सिर पर अथवा दोनों भौंहों पर नए सीमन्तावर्तक यानी माँग और भँवर जैसे चिह्न करते हैं
english: On the head or on the two eyebrows, new partings and whorls (sīmantāvartaka) make
notes: GROUPING: the object of 'kurvanti' is 'mṛtyum' in unit 54, so this unit appears to continue there. 'sīmantāvartaka' is read as a dvandva 'partings and whorls' (hair-parting-like and whorl-like marks); it could also be one term for whorl-like partings, so the sense is not firm. The Hindi 'चिह्न' is used only to make the Hindi readable and is not in the Sanskrit.

words.gloss: from six nights, after six nights
from three nights, after three nights

hindi: स्वस्थ के लिए छह रात के बाद, किन्तु रोगी के लिए तीन रात के बाद मृत्यु
english: Death, for a healthy person after six nights, but for a sick person after three nights

text_flags.why: possible: printed 'ṣaḍarātrān' has an extra 'a' and 'n' for 't' (ta/na confusion is seen in this print); ablatives of ṣaḍrātra and trirātra fit the sense

notes: GROUPING: 'mṛtyum' is the object of 'kurvanti' in unit 53, so this unit appears to complete that sentence. The ablatives are rendered 'after' (literally 'from'); the text does not say 'within'. Which of the six or three nights counts is not stated.

hindi: जिसकी, स्नान किए और लेप लगाए हुए की, छाती पहले ही बहुत सूख जाती है
english: He whose chest, when he is bathed and anointed, dries up first and greatly
notes: The sentence continues in unit 56 ('while all the limbs are wet ...'). 'pūrvam' = first, before the rest; 'ahead' is also possible. 'snātānuliptasya' is a genitive in the sense 'of one who has bathed and been anointed'.

hindi: सब अंगों के गीले रहते वह आधा मास नहीं जीता
english: While all the limbs are wet, he does not live half a month

text_flags.why: possible: 'ārdva' is not a word; ārdra (wet) fits the sense (limbs still wet while the chest is dry, unit 55); dr/dv confusion is common in this print

notes: Completes unit 55. 'so'rddhamāsaṃ': 'rddh' is the print's spelling of 'rdh' (orthographic normalisation, recorded once book-wide). The locatives are read as 'with all the limbs wet'; 'ārdreṣu' stands for an unstated noun with sarvagātreṣu.

hindi: जिसकी छाती में गर्मी और जठर यानी पेट में अत्यन्त ठण्डक हो
english: He in whose chest there may be heat, and in the belly (jaṭhara) excessive coldness
notes: Part of a sentence that runs into unit 58 ('loose stool and thirst; just as a preta, so is he'). The verb 'bhavet' is stated once; 'in the belly ... excessive coldness' shares it.

hindi: भिन्न यानी टूटा हुआ मल और प्यास; जैसे प्रेत, वैसे ही वह
english: Loose stool (bhinna, literally 'broken') and thirst; as a departed one (preta), just so is he
notes: Continues unit 57. 'tṛṣṇāca' is tṛṣṇā ca with the space missing. 'bhinna purīṣa' is kept literal ('broken' stool); the modern sense (loose or watery stool) is probable but not stated. 'preta' = a departed one, a dead person. Copula understood.

hindi: मूत्र, मल, निष्ठ्यूत यानी थूक और शुक्र यानी वीर्य पानी में डूबते हैं
english: Urine, stool, spittle (niṣṭhyūta) and semen (śukra) sink in water
notes: Four neuter subjects with one singular verb (taken together). 'apsu' = locative plural of ap (water), regular. The line does not say whose; the sense is of the person described in the surrounding units. niṣṭhyūta = spat-out matter, sputum.

hindi: या जिसका निष्ठ्यूत यानी थूक अनेक रंगों का हो, वह मासों में नष्ट हो जाता है
english: Or he whose spittle (niṣṭhyūta) is of many colours perishes in months

text_flags.why: possible: 'māsān' (accusative plural) gives 'months' with no number; 'māsāt' (after a month) also fits the metre (16 syllables); the printed reading is kept in words

notes: The first 'vā' (or) links this to the signs of unit 59. 'māsān' is accusative plural, 'for/through months', with no number stated; the Hindi 'मासों में' is the plain rendering.

hindi: स्वर की दुर्बलता को और बल तथा वर्ण यानी रंग की हानि को
english: The weakening of the voice and the loss of strength and colour (varṇa)
notes: The object of 'dṛṣṭvā' in unit 62; the two units form one sentence. 'varṇa' is colour or complexion; 'colour' is the plain rendering.

hindi: बिना युक्ति के रोग की वृद्धि को भी देखकर मृत्यु बता दे
english: And having seen the increase of disease without reason (ayuktyā), one should foretell death
notes: Completes unit 61 (the signs seen are the weakening of the voice, the loss of strength and colour, and the increase of disease). 'ayuktyā' is literally 'without (proper) reason, unreasonably'; the sense might also be 'by improper means'. The agent of 'ādiśet' is not stated, so 'one'.

hindi: बिगड़े स्वर में बोलते हुए को, अपनी मृत्यु प्राप्त हुई
english: One speaking in a faulty voice (apasvara), his own death having arrived
notes: GROUPING: units 63 and 64 appear to form one sentence ('parivarjayet', unit 64, probably governs the accusatives here); this is not stated as fact. The grammar of 'prāptaṃ maraṇam ātmanaḥ' is not firm: 'prāptam' may qualify the person (accusative) or agree with 'maraṇam' ('his own death having been reached'). The translation keeps the second reading.

hindi: और इसके शब्द के श्रोता को दूर से ही त्याग दे
english: And one should avoid from afar the hearer of his sound
notes: GROUPING: units 63-64 appear to be one sentence. 'cāsyaśabdasya' is read ca + asya + śabdasya ('of this/his sound'); another division, ca + āsya-śabdasya ('of the sound of the mouth'), gives the same letters and cannot be excluded. Who is meant by 'the hearer' is not clear from the line; the translation stays literal. The agent of 'parivarjayet' is not stated ('one').

words.gloss: one whose groins are afflicted by pain

hindi: जिसकी साँस ऊपर की ओर चढ़ती है, जिसकी गर्मी चली गई है और जिसके वंक्षण यानी जाँघ के जोड़ पीड़ा से पीड़ित हैं, उसको
english: One with upward breath (ūrdhvaśvāsa), whose warmth has gone, whose groins are afflicted by pain
notes: Accusatives; the verb 'parivarjayet' is in unit 66, which these appear to continue into. 'ūrdhvaśvāsa' is literally 'upward breath' (a laboured, upward-rising breath; the modern term is not fixed here). 'vaṅkṣaṇa' = groin (standard). 'śūla' = pain.

words.gram: pres. part. a-adhi-√gam, m. acc. sg.

hindi: और सुख न पाने वाले को बुद्धिमान् त्याग दे
english: And one finding no comfort (śarma): the intelligent one should avoid
notes: Completes unit 65 (the persons described there and here are the objects of 'parivarjayet'). The Sanskrit does not say who the intelligent one is, so none is named.

words.gloss: one in whom cold pustules have arisen

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, जिसके शीत पिटक यानी ठण्डी फुंसियाँ उत्पन्न हुई हैं, अथवा जिसके अंग ठण्डे हैं, वह जलता है
english: On a conjectural reading: he in whom cold pustules (piṭaka) have arisen, or who is cold-limbed, and who burns

text_flags.why: possible: the printed Devanagari 'विद्ह्यते' is not a valid word; 'vidahyate' (burns, is inflamed) is a close reading and suits 'cold limbs' (inner burning with cold limbs); 'vidhyate' (is pierced) is the other possibility

notes: The verb is damaged in print: the IAST 'vidhyate' (is pierced) is a valid form but the printed Devanagari is 'विद्ह्यते'; the translation adopts 'vidahyate' only on a conjectural reading, so confidence is low. 'piṭaka' = pustule, boil. 'śīta-piṭaka' read as 'cold pustules' (the text gives no further detail). The sentence runs on into unit 68.

words.gloss: within the range of the lord of the departed (probably Yama)

hindi: गर्मी से द्वेष करने वाला और ठण्ड से पीड़ित, वह प्रेतों के अधिपति, सम्भवतः यम, की पहुँच में है
english: Hating heat and afflicted by cold, he is within the reach of the lord of the departed (probably Yama)
notes: Completes unit 67. 'pretādhipa' = lord of the departed; Yama is the usual identification (probable). 'gocara' = range, domain. Copula understood ('he is').

hindi: जिसके कण्ठ पर रस्सी जैसी छाया लगी हुई दिखाई देती है
english: He on whose neck a shadow like a rope is seen attached
notes: The sentence is completed in unit 70 (he is dragged by Yama's servants). 'chāyā' = shadow (also 'lustre'); 'shadow' is the plain rendering.

hindi: वह प्राणी निश्चय ही शीघ्र यम के सेवकों द्वारा खींच लिया जाता है
english: That living being is surely dragged away soon by the servants of Yama
notes: Completes unit 69. 'kṛṣyate' is a passive, 'is dragged' (pulled).

words.gloss: concerned with knowing abnormal limbs (name of the chapter)

hindi: इस प्रकार विकृताङ्गविज्ञानीय नामक नवम अध्याय
english: Thus the ninth chapter, named Vikṛtāṅgavijñānīya
notes: Colophon. 'vikṛtāṅgavijñānīya' is kept as the chapter's name; it is formed from vikṛta (abnormal), aṅga (limb or part) and vijñānīya (concerning knowledge). The leading '||' is kept as a token.
